title: Content Writing
intro: Writing bots are the easiest thing to build and the hardest to keep, which is why the catalogues carry many and people talk about few. The ones that survive are not general writing assistants but narrow ones: turning a call into a post, repurposing something long into something short, holding a calendar and drafting against it. The constraint that matters is voice, and it is the thing most templates handle worst. A bot given three examples produces something recognisably yours; a bot given a topic produces something recognisably nobody's. If a listing does not ask for samples of your existing writing, that tells you what the output will read like. Also worth noting: several bots in this category will publish directly. That is a much larger decision than drafting, and worth making deliberately rather than by accepting a default.

bots.fitReason: A dedicated rewrite desk for posts, emails, blogs and DMs that aims at human-sounding voice, and it stays draft-only so nothing gets published behind your back. Rewrites what you give it rather than generating from a cold topic, so you need a first pass of your own.
Diagnoses one X account and writes the next post in that account's voice, plus the lines to cut. Narrow by design: it edits and drafts for a single account, not a general content pipeline.
Draft-only X desk for one named account: it writes posts and never publishes them, which is the right default. It deliberately does not research the feed, so the ideas have to come from you.

Five roles — idea scout, hook writer, calendar planner, competitor analyst, mention watcher — so drafting happens against a calendar rather than at random. More machinery than a solo poster needs, and voice depends on what you feed the hook writer.

Turns what you save on X into a weekly thread drafted in your voice — repurposing from your own material, which is the format that actually holds voice. Only does the Saturday roundup; no daily posting.

Learns voice from the owner's existing X profile and recommends one tweet plus replies each weekday, which is a real calendar habit rather than a topic generator. Single brand, single platform, recommendations only.
One HQ chat that picks the angle and drafts in your voice, sending nothing without a go. Tuned to a builder's Grok-on-X tone, so if that is not your register you will be fighting it.

Writes Instagram carousel copy slide by slide plus the caption, then hands a brief to a companion art bot. Portuguese-language and Instagram-only, and it assumes the rest of that content chain exists.
